title: Microsoft will be carbon negative by 2030
text:
While the world will need to reach net zero, those of us who can afford to move faster and go further should do so. That's why today we are announcing an ambitious goal and a new plan to reduce and ultimately remove Microsoft's carbon footprint.

By 2030 Microsoft will be carbon negative, and by 2050 Microsoft will remove from the environment all the carbon the company has emitted either directly or by electrical consumption since it was founded in 1975.

We recognize that progress requires not just a bold goal but a detailed plan. As described below, we are launching today an aggressive program to cut our carbon emissions by more than half by 2030, both for our direct emissions and for our entire supply and value chain. We will fund this in part by expanding our internal carbon fee, in place since 2012 and increased last year, to start charging not only our direct emissions, but those from our supply and value chains.

We are also launching an initiative to use Microsoft technology to help our suppliers and customers around the world reduce their own carbon footprints and a new $1 billion climate innovation fund to accelerate the global development of carbon reduction, capture, and removal technologies. Beginning next year, we will also make carbon reduction an explicit aspect of our procurement processes for our supply chain. Our progress on all of these fronts will be published in a new annual Environmental Sustainability Report that will detail our carbon impact and reduction journey.

Taking responsibility for our carbon footprint. We will take responsibility for all our emissions, so by 2030 we can cut them by more than half and remove more carbon than we emit each year. Investing for new carbon reduction and removal technology. We will deploy $1 billion of our own capital in a new Climate Innovation Fund to accelerate the development of carbon reduction and removal technologies that will help us and the world become carbon negative. Ensuring effective transparency. We will publish an annual Environmental Sustainability Report that provides transparency on our progress, based on strong global reporting standards.

title: Apple commits to be 100 percent carbon neutral for its supply chain and products by 2030
text:
Cupertino, California — Apple today unveiled its plan to become carbon neutral across its entire business, manufacturing supply chain, and product life cycle by 2030. The company is already carbon neutral today for its global corporate operations, and this new commitment means that by 2030, every Apple device sold will have net zero climate impact.

Apple is providing detail on its approach to carbon neutrality with a roadmap for other companies, as industries look to reduce their impact on climate change. In its 2020 Environmental Progress Report — released today — Apple details its plans to reduce emissions by 75 percent by 2030 while developing innovative carbon removal solutions for the remaining 25 percent of its comprehensive footprint.

Low carbon product design: Apple will continue to increase the use of low carbon and recycled materials in its products, innovate in product recycling, and design products to be as energy efficient as possible. Apple decreased its carbon footprint by 4.3 million metric tons in 2019 through design and recycled content innovations in its products. Over the past 11 years, Apple has reduced the average energy needed for product use by 73 percent.

Expanding energy efficiency: Apple will identify new ways to lower energy use at its corporate facilities and help its supply chain make the same transition. The number of facilities participating in Apple's Supplier Energy Efficiency Program grew to 92 in 2019; these facilities avoided over 779,000 annualized metric tons of supply chain carbon emissions. Last year, Apple invested in energy efficiency upgrades to over 6.4 million square feet of new and existing buildings, lowering electricity needs by nearly one-fifth and saving the company $27 million.

Renewable energy: Apple will remain at 100 percent renewable energy for its operations — focusing on creating new projects and moving its entire supply chain to clean power. Apple now has commitments from over 70 suppliers to use 100 percent renewable energy for Apple production — equivalent to nearly 8 gigawatts in commitments to power the manufacturing of its products. Once completed, these commitments will avoid over 14.3 million metric tons of CO2e annually — the equivalent of taking more than 3 million cars off the road each year.

title: Sustainability — By the Numbers
text:
In a world being reshaped by climate change, Nike is relentlessly innovating at scale to help all athletes perform at their best.

By the Numbers. Sixty-nine percent reduction of absolute Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions from Nike Operations in FY24, compared to a FY20 baseline. Thirty-six percent reduction of absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions from Nike's manufacturing and transportation in FY24, versus a FY20 baseline. Ninety-six percent of electricity consumption in Nike's global operations was sourced from renewable electricity in FY24. One hundred percent of operational waste was diverted from landfill by Nike's strategic finished goods suppliers in FY24, with over 60 percent reused or recycled. Less than 1 percent of inbound air freight was used to move Nike goods in FY24. A more than 40 percent reduction in freshwater consumption by Nike's material manufacturing suppliers was achieved over the past decade.

That is why NIKE is focused on sustainable innovation at scale across our entire business. From industry-leading apparel technology, like Dri-FIT, to footwear breakthroughs like ReactX foam, we continue to push the known limits of product design, always challenging ourselves to create better. We don't settle for anything less than high performance products, made more sustainably, that help athletes adapt and perform at their best.

Across our entire value chain, a network of thousands of suppliers and partners, and millions of athletes worldwide, we drive continuous improvement in how we design, make and deliver products to help reduce emissions and eliminate waste. We work across industries and continents to conserve water resources and develop cleaner chemistries that help minimize environmental impact. We take action every day as only NIKE can to move the world forward through sport and help every athlete thrive.

title: The Climate Crisis Is Our Business — Climate Goals
text:
The climate crisis is an existential threat, and every part of Patagonia's business is implicated. We must radically reduce carbon emissions by transforming how we make our products. We must also double down on our work to help communities get off fossil fuels and protect nature, the original climate solution. And we must demand nothing short of systemic change from government and industry. The fight is on every front.

Carbon Neutral Is Not Enough. Purchasing offsets to get to carbon neutral doesn't erase the footprint we create and won't save us in the long run. If our goal was to cut emissions from our owned and operated stores, offices and distribution centers, we'd be good. But the bulk of our emissions — nearly 99% — comes from our supply chain and materials manufacturing. We take responsibility for all of it.

How We Hold Ourselves Accountable. We have set ambitious goals across our company and our network of partners in alignment with a set of standards provided by the Science Based Targets Initiative (SBTi). SBTi has a robust target-setting and validation process that our company underwent giving us confidence that our goals align with the latest science and the 2015 Paris Agreement's commitment to limit warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius. SBTi uses three "scopes" or areas of a business to help companies like ours focus their efforts.

Here is what we signed up for. Near-Term, FY2030: Reduce absolute Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions 80% by FY2030 from a FY2017 base year. Reduce absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions from purchased goods and services, upstream transportation and distribution, business travel and downstream transportation and distribution 55% by FY2030 from a FY2017 base year. Long-Term, FY2040: Reduce absolute Scope 1, 2, and 3 GHG emissions 90% by FY2040 from a FY2017 base year. Commit to reach net-zero GHG emissions across the value chain by FY2040 from a FY2017 base year.

We acknowledge that the latest science may change, and Patagonia is committed to adapting to the most robust targets to do our part in keeping warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius. While target language may change over time, our ambition and focus on cutting absolute greenhouse gas emissions will not.

org: Glowline Appliances Inc. (invented company — not a real business)
title: Our Climate Commitments
text:
Glowline Appliances Inc. is committed to reducing its environmental footprint across every stage of the product lifecycle. Our Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions will fall by 42% by 2028, compared to a 2019 baseline, validated under the Science Based Targets initiative's Corporate Net-Zero Standard. This target was approved by our Sustainability Committee in March 2024 and will be reported annually alongside our GHG Protocol-aligned inventory.

Beyond direct operations, we are working with our supply chain to halve embodied carbon in our products by the end of the decade. We believe smarter manufacturing and better materials will get us there, and we are proud of the progress our teams have already made.

Our Chief Sustainability Officer will oversee a 15,000 MWh reduction in facility energy use by 2027, relative to a 2021 baseline, as part of our TCFD-aligned climate disclosures. We also aim to eliminate 3,200 metric tons of packaging waste annually by 2026.

We know our customers care about the planet, and so do we. Glowline will keep innovating toward a cleaner tomorrow, guided by our values and our commitment to doing the right thing for the communities where we operate.

Water use across our three largest manufacturing sites will drop 18% by 2029 against a 2018 base year, overseen by our Executive Committee, and independently assured under ISO 14064. We will not purchase carbon offsets to claim neutrality before we have exhausted direct reduction opportunities within our own operations and supply chain.

org: Cobalt Ridge Mining Corp (invented company — not a real business)
title: Environmental Responsibility Statement
text:
Cobalt Ridge Mining Corp recognizes the climate impact of resource extraction and is taking steps to address it responsibly. By 2035, we aim to cut Scope 1 emissions from our processing facilities by 60%, using 2015 as our baseline year, in line with the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard. Our board of directors reviews progress against this target twice a year.

We are also exploring renewable power purchase agreements that could supply up to 400 GWh of clean electricity annually to our largest site by 2030. No baseline has been set for this figure yet, and the agreements remain under negotiation.

Cobalt Ridge is proud to support the communities near our operations and will continue to invest in local environmental restoration projects. We believe in leaving the land better than we found it, and our teams take this responsibility seriously every day.

Net-zero across our full value chain, including Scope 3 emissions from downstream processing, remains our long-term ambition. We have not yet set an interim target year for this goal, pending further study by our sustainability committee.

Tailings pond methane capture will be expanded to triple current capture rates by 2027. The chief financial officer has approved capital funding for this expansion, and independent verification will follow CDP disclosure guidelines starting with our 2026 reporting cycle.

org: Driftwood Apparel Co. (invented company — not a real business)
title: Sustainability at Driftwood
text:
Driftwood Apparel Co. believes fashion can be a force for good. We are dedicated to protecting the planet for future generations through every collection we design and every fiber we source.

Our science-based target, validated by the Science Based Targets initiative, commits us to reducing absolute Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions 46% by 2030 from a 2022 baseline. This target was approved by our executive leadership team and is reported each year in our sustainability disclosures aligned with the ISSB IFRS S2 standard.

We are also working toward using 100% recycled polyester across our product line, a goal we hope to reach as soon as possible. We are incredibly proud of the momentum behind this initiative and the passion our design teams bring to sustainable materials.

By 2032, we will reduce water intensity in our dyeing processes by 35% against a 2020 base year, overseen by our head of sustainability and verified under ISO 14064. We also hope to halve emissions from inbound transportation by the end of the decade, though this goal has not yet been validated by a third party.

Driftwood will continue to be a caring, responsible steward of the environment, and we invite our customers to join us on this journey toward a better, greener future for everyone.

org: Ferrous & Vine Foods Group (invented company — not a real business)
title: Building a Sustainable Food System
text:
Ferrous & Vine Foods Group is committed to building a more sustainable food system. Our Audit Committee has approved a target to cut Scope 3 emissions from agricultural sourcing by 28% by 2031, measured against a 2021 baseline, consistent with the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard and reported under CDP.

We are proud to be doing our part for the planet, and we believe every small step counts. Our teams across the business are energized by this mission and are finding new ways to reduce waste every day.

Packaging emissions will fall by 500,000 metric tons annually by 2028, a commitment overseen by our chief executive officer and independently assured against the Corporate Net-Zero Standard. We also intend to source 100% of our palm oil from certified deforestation-free suppliers, though we have not yet committed to a target year for full transition.

Our ambition is to achieve net-zero emissions across our entire value chain, a goal our board of directors fully supports. In the meantime, we will keep listening to our customers and communities as we shape what comes next.

Refrigerant-related emissions at our largest distribution centers will be reduced 22% by 2027 relative to a 2019 baseline, verified under ISO 14064 and reported annually alongside our TCFD-aligned climate disclosures.
